arxiv-2111-05780.creator: Ahmad Biniaz, Anil Maheshwari, Michiel Smid
arxiv-2111-05780.description: Abstract We present approximation algorithms for the following NP-hard optimization problems related to bottleneck spanning trees in metric spaces. 1. The disjoint bottleneck spanning tree problem: Given n n pairs of points in a metric space, find two disjoint trees each containing exactly one point from each pair and minimize the largest edge length (over all edges of both trees).

arxiv-2206-00234.title: Assessing Group-level Gender Bias in Professional Evaluations: The Case of Medical Student End-of-Shift Feedback
arxiv-2206-00234.creator: Emmy Liu, Michael Henry Tessler, Nicole Dubosh, Katherine Mosher Hiller, Roger P. Levy
arxiv-2206-00234.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Emmy Liu, Michael Henry Tessler, Nicole Dubosh, Katherine Mosher Hiller, Roger P. Levy. Although approximately 50% of medical school graduates today are women, female physicians tend to be underrepresented in senior positions, make less money than their male counterparts and receive fewer promotions. There is a growing body of literature demonstrating gender bias in various forms of evaluation in medicine, but this work was mainly conducted by looking for specific words using fixed dictionaries such as LIWC and focused on recommendation letters.

arxiv-2210-16298.title: Investigating Ensemble Methods for Model Robustness Improvement of Text Classifiers
arxiv-2210-16298.creator: Jieyu Zhao, Xuezhi Wang, Yao Qin, Jilin Chen, Kai-Wei Chang
arxiv-2210-16298.description: Abstract Large pre-trained language models have shown remarkable performance over the past few years. These models, however, sometimes learn superficial features from the dataset and cannot generalize to the distributions that are dissimilar to the training scenario. There have been several approaches proposed to reduce model’s reliance on these bias features which can improve model robustness in the out-of-distribution setting.

arxiv-2305-01110.title: Upwards Tropospheric Influence on Tropical Stratospheric Upwelling Under peer review
arxiv-2305-01110.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by . The steady response of the stratosphere to a sea surface temperature (SST) forcing is considered in two separate theoretical models. It is first shown that anomalies in SST impose a geopotential anomaly at the tropopause. Solutions to the linearized quasi-geostrophic potential vorticity equations are then used to show that the vertical length scale of a tropopause geopotential anomaly is initially shallow, but significantly increased by diabatic heating from radiative relaxation. This process is a quasi-balanced response of the stratosphere to tropospheric forcing.

arxiv-2509-05989.title: Simulation of Solar Surface Flux Transport Constrained by Magnetic Power Spectra. I. Flux Transport Parameter
arxiv-2509-05989.creator: Yukun Luo, Jie Jiang, Ruihui Wang
arxiv-2509-05989.description: Abstract The multi-scale structure of the solar surface magnetic field is essential for understanding both the Sun’s internal dynamo processes and its external magnetic activity. The surface flux transport (SFT) model has been successful in describing the large-scale evolution of the surface field, but its ability to capture observed multi-scale features, quantified by magnetic power spectra, remains uncertain.

arxiv-2512-03950.title: Collective dynamics of trail-interacting particles
arxiv-2512-03950.creator: Paul Pineau, Samuel Bell, Raphaël Voituriez, Ram M. Adar
arxiv-2512-03950.description: Abstract Trail interactions occur when past particle trajectories bias future motion, rendering the system out of thermodynamic equilibrium. While such systems are abundant in nature, their understanding is limited to the single-particle level or phenomenological mean-field theories. Here, we introduce a minimal model of many trail-interacting particles that extends this paradigm to the fluctuating collective level.

BackgroundLittle is known about parental awareness of multisystem inflammatory syndrome in children (MIS-C), a rare but severe sequela of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) infection.MethodsVia a nationally representative, cross-sectional survey of US parents conducted via Ipsos KnowledgePanel from October to November 2021, we used bivariate and multivariable analyses to describe and identify demographic variables associated with parental knowledge of and attitudes toward MIS-C and to examine associations with perceived coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) severity and susceptibility.ResultsResponse rate was 64.2% (3230/5034).

pmc-13096861.description: The peripheral myelin protein P2 (also known as PMP2/FABP8) has two basic functions in vivo: the transport of fatty acids within the cell to the target compartments and the adhesion of lipid bilayers in the peripheral nervous system myelin to each other.
